lesson.text: Quick memory: what should you do if something online upsets you? (Stop, and tell a grown-up you trust.) Today: screens and balance.
Screens can be great: games, learning, and video calls with family. But a healthy day has lots of different things in it.
A balanced day has sleep, food, moving and playing outside, time with family and friends, learning, rest, and some screen time.
Notice how you feel. Too long on screens can give you tired eyes, a sore neck, grumpiness or trouble sleeping. That is your body saying “time for a break”.
Screens just before bed can make it harder to fall asleep, so many families switch them off about an hour before bedtime.
Stop at a good moment: the end of a level, a finished build, or bedtime in the game. When your player sleeps, this game gives you a STOP FOR TODAY button.
Rest your eyes: every 20 minutes, look at something far away for about 20 seconds.
Try it in the world: when night comes in your world, let it be your signal to take a break. Do something off-screen, like reading or playing outside.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: screen time or off-screen time?
exercises.explain: Screen time: the game, the cartoon, the video call. Off-screen: the bike, the book, the den.

exercises.prompt: A balanced day has many different activities, not only screens.
exercises.hint: Think of all the parts of a day.
exercises.explain: True: sleep, food, play outside, family, learning, rest and some screen time make a balanced day.

exercises.prompt: Your eyes feel tired after playing. What is the best thing to do?
choices: take a break and look far away
rub your eyes and keep going
exercises.explain: Take a break and look at something far away to rest your eyes.

exercises.prompt: Which is a good time to stop playing?
exercises.hint: Look for a natural stopping place.
choices: at the end of a level or a finished build
in the middle of a boss fight
only when the battery runs out
exercises.explain: The end of a level or a finished build is a good moment to stop.

exercises.prompt: Why is it a good idea to switch off screens before bed?
exercises.hint: Think about how you fall asleep.
choices: screens can make it harder to fall asleep
exercises.explain: Screens just before bed can keep you awake, so switching off helps you sleep.

exercises.prompt: Match each feeling to what might help.
matches: look far away for a while
take a break and play outside
exercises.hint: What does each part of your body need?
exercises.explain: Tired eyes: look far away. Stiff neck: stretch. Grumpy: a break outside. Can't sleep: no screens before bed.

exercises.prompt: Feeling grumpy after a long time on screens can be a sign that you need a break.
exercises.hint: Listen to your body and your feelings.
exercises.explain: True: grumpiness can be your body saying it is time for a break.

exercises.prompt: Bram has 1 hour of screen time today. He has used 35 minutes. How many minutes are left?
exercises.hint: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Take away what he has used.
exercises.explain: 1 hour is 60 minutes, and 60 − 35 = 25 minutes are left.

exercises.prompt: What should you do every 20 minutes on a screen?
exercises.hint: Remember the lesson card about resting your eyes.
choices: look at something far away for about 20 seconds
exercises.explain: Every 20 minutes, look at something far away for about 20 seconds.

exercises.prompt: Tilly's plan for Saturday: put it in time order, from morning to night.
exercises.explain: 8:00 breakfast, 10:00 the park, 12:30 lunch, 15:00 games, 19:00 bath, book and bed.

exercises.prompt: Which day is the most balanced?
exercises.hint: Look for lots of different things.
choices: school, play outside, some games, a book, bed
exercises.explain: The first day has learning, play, some games, reading and sleep: balanced.

exercises.prompt: Zara wants to stop playing but finds it hard. What might help her?
exercises.hint: What could she decide before she starts playing, like when she will stop?
choices: decide a stopping point before she starts
start a new level every time
exercises.explain: Deciding a stopping point before she starts, like the end of a level, makes stopping easier.

exercises.prompt: Some screen time, like a video call with family or a lesson in the School, can be good for you.
exercises.explain: True: screens can help us learn and stay close to family. Balance is what matters.

exercises.prompt: How can you tell your body needs a break from screens?
choices: tired eyes, a sore neck or feeling grumpy
exercises.explain: Tired eyes, a sore neck or grumpiness are signs you need a break.

exercises.prompt: When your player sleeps in this game, what button helps you stop?
exercises.hint: Remember the lesson card about stopping at a good moment.
exercises.explain: STOP FOR TODAY: when your player sleeps, the game offers it as a good moment to stop.

exercises.prompt: Every 20 minutes on a screen, you look far away for 20 seconds. How many seconds of looking far away is that in 1 hour?
exercises.hint: First find how many lots of 20 minutes are in an hour.
exercises.explain: 1 hour is 60 minutes, and 60 ÷ 20 = 3 breaks. Each break is 20 seconds: 3 × 20 = 60 seconds, a whole minute of rest for your eyes.
